preamble: No documented case of an aspirated stop [tʰ] becoming a palatalized [tʲ] was found. The example formerly given here, a supposed aspirated stage in Russian or Slavic, is unfounded: Slavic languages have no aspirated stops, and Slavic secondary palatalization affected plain *t before front vowels (t > tʲ).

examples.note: Palatalization before a front vowel applied to plain /t/; no aspirated stage existed, so this belongs under t_to_t_palatalized.

sources: Timberlake, A. (2004). A Reference Grammar of Russian. Cambridge University Press.
